PullRequest.Title: Markdown: do not reuse the preview script nonce and escape failed math
PullRequest.Body: Two independent hardening changes to how Markdown HTML is rendered. ### Markdown preview: do not let content scripts reuse the preview script nonce - `domEval` re-creates scripts from rendered content so they run when the preview's CSP allows them. It no longer copies a `nonce` attribute from the content, so content cannot opt into the nonce of the preview's own scripts. ### Markdown math: escape failed math and limit math rules to renderer-generated HTML - Math that KaTeX fails to render is now shown as escaped text. Its raw source used to be inserted as HTML, also for Markdown without HTML support, where the math sanitizer rules then allowed arbitrary classes and math styles on it. - In chat, math is rendered, and its broader `class` and `style` sanitizer rules are applied, only for Markdown that does not support raw HTML. Markdown with `supportHtml` gets the base attribute rules and shows math as text. - The base attribute rules keep `class="code"` on the renderer's `div[data-code]` code block placeholders; the math rules allowed it before. - Inline `position` in math styles is limited to `relative`. ### How to test - Markdown preview: open a Markdown file with lists, code blocks, and math in the preview. Edit the file while the preview is visible and check that the preview updates. Preview script contributions still load. - Chat: render a response containing math (`$\frac{1}{2}$`, `$$…$$` blocks) with `chat.math.enabled`. Check that math renders and copies. Check that `$\undefinedcommand x$` shows as text, and that code block pills in responses keep their spacing. ### Validation - `node --test extensions/markdown-language-features/scripts/previewCsp.browser.test.mts` (new): **passed** (1/1). It checks that content scripts carrying the real nonce do not run in either update path, and fails without the preview change. - `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/markdown/test/browser/markdownKatexSupport.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatMarkdownRenderer.test.ts --run src/vs/base/test/browser/markdownRenderer.test.ts --run src/vs/base/test/browser/domSanitize.test.ts`: **passed** (323 passing, 2 pending). The new tests for failed math and code block placeholder classes fail without the change. - `pnpm run typecheck-client`: **passed**. The `preview-src` project type check: **passed**. - `pnpm run eslint` on the changed files: **passed**. - Checked manually in Code OSS: the Markdown preview (including live updates while editing), and chat responses with math, failed math, and `supportHtml`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or live-update a Markdown preview containing contributed scripts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial display parses and appends rendered HTML, while live updates parse then replace or morph the preview DOM; domEval synchronously walks script descendants and recreates each script before update completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recreated script elements may fetch their existing src URLs when permitted by CSP.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one browser load per recreated external script in the initial or changed subtree, subject to CSP and browser cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: domEval already recreated every script and preserved src; the diff only stops copying nonce, so it cannot add a fetch and may prevent a content script from loading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Inline script activation is synchronous with DOM insertion; external fetch completion is browser-managed and not explicitly awaited by preview reconciliation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of script elements in the initial preview or DOM subtree added by a content update.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One webview message/update is processed on the browser event loop; external script loading remains browser-scheduled and is not made more concurrent by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Browser HTTP/resource caching is unchanged; there is no new application cache or miss path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all domEval call sites and the recreated attributes were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Contributed script count and browser cache state vary, but the changed attribute list removes work and does not increase cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the change removes one copied attribute from existing per-script work and introduces no new DOM traversal or boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and progressively update chat Markdown with math enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each render synchronously decides whether math is safe, configures marked and DOMPurify, parses/sanitizes the full Markdown, constructs DOM, and performs math/table post-processing before the content part is usable. The new case-insensitive span check is a linear scan only for trusted HTML-disabled content and is followed by the pre-existing full parse/sanitize pass.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Lazy AMD loading of the bundled KaTeX module.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced module load per process because all callers share a Lazy promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: With chat math enabled, the constructor already initiated the same shared KaTeX load and re-rendered when it completed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first content part initially renders without KaTeX, then re-renders after the existing asynchronous load; it does not block initial chat content display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Append a link for the bundled KaTeX stylesheet, causing the browser to load the resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one stylesheet element per document, guarded by querySelector('link.katex') and browser caching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every existing getExtension/loadExtension path already called ensureKatexStyles with the same per-document guard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Style application can affect final math layout but the link insertion is not newly added or increased by this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Markdown character count, number of streaming render passes, number and size of math tokens, and number of generated class/style attributes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering runs serially on the UI event loop. Streaming may reconstruct or morph a part repeatedly, but no new parallel work or unbounded queue is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: KaTeX module loading is positively cached and in-flight-coalesced by Lazy; stylesheet insertion is guarded per document. The diff does not change either cache lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor, incremental callback, renderer invocation, KaTeX cache, and stylesheet guard were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very long streamed responses increase the added scan's absolute CPU, but it remains one simple linear pass inside an existing render that already parses and sanitizes the same full string.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added scan and branch checks are bounded local CPU work dominated by existing full rendering, while unsafe HTML cases now skip KaTeX rendering and its broader sanitizer work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render successful or failed KaTeX expressions and sanitize renderer-generated HTML
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Successful tokens run KaTeX, encode the source attribute, and now replace dollar signs; failed tokens catch KaTeX errors and now escape the raw token before the existing HTML parse/sanitize. Attribute sanitization performs one additional constant-time position/class condition within existing callbacks.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and total source length of math tokens plus number of class/style attributes emitted by KaTeX or Markdown rendering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Token rendering and sanitization are synchronous and serial within one Markdown render.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved in per-token encoding or fallback escaping; the shared KaTeX module cache is covered by the chat-render scenario.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both renderer branches and DOMPurify predicate invocation were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Adversarially large or numerous invalid formulas increase allocation linearly, but escaping is one bounded pass after already attempting KaTeX and is necessary to produce the new safe output semantics.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added work is linear/constant within already more expensive token rendering and sanitization, with no higher-order scaling, retention, or new boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files and every diff page. Traced preview initialization/live updates, chat construction and streaming re-renders, sanitizer predicate execution, KaTeX success/failure paths, shared module loading, and stylesheet insertion. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
